items.zh_full: 极光是自然界最壮观的灯光秀之一：它看起来像绿色或红色的帷幕在夜空中飘动。从地面观看时，这种色彩斑斓的展示似乎遥远且与地球表面发生的任何事情无关。然而，极光实际上是由太空天气驱动的——太阳风携带的带电粒子与地球磁场相互作用，沿着磁力线进入高层大气，激发氧原子和氮原子发光，形成绿色或红色的极光。这些粒子注入大气的同时，也会在地球表面感应出电流，可能对电网造成威胁。太空天气事件（如日冕物质抛射）会增强太阳风，导致地磁暴，进而可能引发电网电压波动、变压器损坏甚至大规模停电。因此，极光不仅是美丽的自然现象，也是太空天气影响地面基础设施的可见标志。

items.title: Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves Probing Phase Transitions in the Standard Model and Beyond
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are unique messengers of physics in the early Universe and possible sources for the observed data from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). It has been demonstrated that SIGWs have the potential to probe cosmological phase transitions via measurement of the equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath, which have non-trivial time dependence during phase transitions. In this work, we improve on existing studies of SIGWs in a time-dependent background with time-dependent initial conditions and an entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model (SM). We provide possible physical explanations for features of the gravitational wave spectrum from phase transitions, the most prominent of which for a scale-invariant curvature spectrum is a step due to entropy dilution. We show that current and future gravitational wave observations across a wide range of frequencies can probe phase transitions in the SM and physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Signals from the QCD crossover appear around 10 nHz, inside the observable window of PTAs. We perform data analyses using NANOGrav 15-year data, showing a mild preference for the QCD crossover over standard radiation domination for two choices of curvature spectra. BSM phase transitions in the TeV range lead to signals around mHz, which are accessible in future space-based experiments such as LISA, Taiji and TianQin.

items.title: Earth's Gravity May Have Kept the Early Moon's Volcanic Heart Beating
items.summary: We typically think of the Moon as a static, floating object that has remained the same for basically its entire lifetime, with an occasional asteroid impact serving as an exception. That understanding is grounded in physics - the Moon should have cooled rapidly after forming when a huge protoplanet hit the early Earth around 4.5 billion years ago. But, some lunar material returned from the Chang’e-5 mission was notably formed only around two billion years ago, yet appeared to be volcanic in origin. So how did a world that was supposed to have settled down without volcanism remain hot enough to create these materials more than two billion years after its violent birth? A new paper from Miao Chen of the Chengdu University of Technology and his colleagues, and recently published in the journal Planet, offers an explanation - tidal heating.

items.title: Ultra-Heavy Dark Matter Through Exponential Production Mechanism
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13842v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exponential production of dark matter has been introduced recently as one of the alternatives to the widely studied thermal production of dark matter scenarios. This non-thermal production mechanism leads to the exponential growth in the abundance of the dark matter ($\chi$) through its scatterings with the bath particle ($\xi$), viz. $\chi + \xi \to \chi + \chi$. In our framework, we consider a scalar dark matter $\chi$ charged under $Z_3$ symmetry and bath particle $\xi$ to be standard model singlet and determine the maximum mass of the dark matter using the criteria of perturbativity. We find that dark matter has an upper mass around the ballpark of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15})$ GeV for the cases when the bath particle mass is similar to the dark matter mass. The computations are largely performed with minimal model dependence and will hold in any scenario where the renormalizable couplings driving the exponential growth effectively reduce to $\chi^3\xi$ interactions. Thus, in exponential production of dark matter, we have a possibility of an ultra-heavy dark matter with large couplings, making the scenario phenomenologically interesting. Later, we extend the simplified dark matter model to a UV-complete Dirac Type-I seesaw model where the $Z_3$ symmetry is obtained as a residual unbroken subgroup of a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, providing a natural connection with the neutrino sector.

items.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-\Gamma H^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $\Gamma={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $\sigma\equiv\Gamma/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $\sigma$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2\sigma/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(\sigma m_\nu^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $\Gamma=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$\Gamma$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $\Gamma\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($\sigma\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.

items.title: The unified bound dark energy--bound dark matter model confronted with DESI DR2, ACT and SPT-3G, and the Unite supernovae measurements
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The unified bound dark energy-bound dark matter (BDE-BDM) model derives the whole dark sector from a single supersymmetric SU(3) dark gauge group, whose lightest meson is the dark energy and whose heavier bound states, created with a velocity $v_c$ when the group condenses, are the dark matter. Because the condensation scale $\Lambda_c$ is fixed by gauge-coupling unification, the dark-energy sector has no free parameter beyond those of $\Lambda$CDM, and the dark-matter sector adds only $v_c$. We confront the model with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), the Planck, ACT DR6 and SPT-3G D1 CMB spectra, the combined ACT and SPT CMB lensing and the Unite supernovae. The measured condensation scale, $\Lambda_c=43.74\pm0.11$ eV, lies inside the window $34^{+16}_{-11}$ eV predicted by unification, and the dark energy thaws without ever crossing the phantom divide, reaching $w_0=-0.9267\pm0.0003$ today; it thus reproduces the DESI distances that $w_0w_a$CDM fits with a phantom past. BDE-BDM gives the best fit to the DESI DR2 BAO of the four models, reducing $\chi^2_{\rm BAO}$ by 20% with respect to $\Lambda$CDM, more than $w_0w_a$CDM, and over the full data combination it is statistically equivalent to both $\Lambda$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM, with $\ln B=-0.50$ and $-0.15$, while having two fewer dark-energy parameters than $w_0w_a$CDM. Within bound dark energy, bound dark matter is moderately preferred over cold dark matter, $\ln B=+3.2$ with $\Delta\chi^2=-9.0$, mostly from the CMB. The data now constrain the bound velocity from both sides, $v_c=0.37\pm0.14$, which places the free-streaming cutoff of the matter power spectrum at $k_{1/2}=1.49\,h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and lowers the amplitude of structure to $S_8=0.807\pm0.007$. Future high-redshift and Lyman-$\alpha$ forest data, together with growth and lensing measurements, will therefore provide the decisive tests of the unified dark sector.

items.title: Stable cosmology under flexible covariances: Rescaling and cross-survey correlations in DESI BAO and supernova data
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combinations of cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), and Type Ia supernova (SN) data currently favor evolving dark energy over $\Lambda$CDM at the $\sim 3$--$4\sigma$ level, making it important to test whether this preference could be driven by imperfectly modeled uncertainties. We introduce a phenomenological framework in which the published covariance of each dataset is rescaled by a free parameter and the SN compilations are allowed effective cross-survey correlations. We apply it to DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 temperature and polarization data, and a joint likelihood of Pantheon+, Union3, and DES-Dovekie constructed on a common redshift basis. The DESI, Union3, and DES-Dovekie data are consistent with their published covariances, while Pantheon+ shows a mild preference for additional covariance. In all cases the data still allow error bars up to $\sim 1.7$ times larger than published at 95% credibility, yet freeing the rescaling parameters improves the best fit by $\Delta\chi^2 < 1$. Pantheon+ and Union3 exhibit a clear positive effective correlation, $r\simeq 0.4$--$0.5$, plausibly reflecting their shared supernovae; the Pantheon+--DES-Dovekie correlation is weaker and model dependent, and the Union3--DES-Dovekie correlation is consistent with zero. The added covariance freedom broadens the cosmological constraints without shifting them: for the full data combination, the improvement of $w_0w_a$CDM over $\Lambda$CDM changes only from $\Delta\chi^2 = 12.8$ to $12.3$ (nominally $3.15\sigma$ to $3.07\sigma$). The preference for evolving dark energy is therefore robust to covariance misestimation of the form considered here.

items.title: Cosmic String Networks with Time-Varying Tension: Field-Theory Simulations and an Analytic Model
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cosmic string networks are predicted in some early-Universe scenarios, and in certain models, the string tension becomes a function of time. Here, for the first time, we perform numerical field-theory simulations of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension in an expanding Universe. We use a modified Abelian-Higgs model in which the tension varies as a power law of the scale factor $a$, that is, $\mu \propto a^{-2m}$. We perform simulations on grids containing $8192^3$ grid points, with $m\in[-0.5,0.5]$, during radiation- and matter-dominated epochs. We find that, in our model, a string network forms only when the potential decreases more slowly than the amplitude of field oscillations redshifts due to the expansion of the Universe. Once formed, the network evolves according to the standard scaling behavior predicted by the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model. To interpret these results, we compare the predictions of the VOS model with time-dependent tension to the asymptotic values obtained from the numerical simulations. Overall, we find good agreement between the numerical field-theory simulations and the calibrated VOS model. These results shed light on the evolution of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension and have potential implications for their observational signatures.

items.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise measurements of galaxy bias parameters are essential for extracting cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Field-level analyses infer bias coefficients at a finite cutoff $\Lambda$, typically related to the lattice resolution, while $n$-point function analyses typically adopt renormalization conditions defined in the low-$k$ limit. In this work, we use the renormalization group (RG) to relate field-level measurements at different cutoffs and connect them to $n$-point function measurements. We generate mock galaxy fields with a Lagrangian perturbation theory forward model and a galaxy bias expansion, and then measure the bias parameters across a range of cutoffs. We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $\Lambda\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_\delta$ and second-order $b_{\delta^2}, b_{{G}_2}$. We also measure the running on halo catalogs based on full $N$-body simulations and show that the RG prediction describes the measurements well within the predicted systematic errors. Our results establish the RG flow as a natural formulation for relating galaxy bias measurements at different cutoffs and connecting the schemes used in field-level and $n$-point function analyses.

items.title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A light scalar present during inflation generically acquires a misalignment and can later constitute the dark matter. Since it fluctuates independently of the inflaton, however, it carries isocurvature perturbations. Isocurvature and overclosure bounds together rule out the simplest version of this scenario at high inflationary scales. We show that a weak coupling to the primordial plasma can relax both bounds simultaneously. The plasma depletes the scalar abundance through thermal damping, a dissipative effect arising from the plasma's finite equilibration time, thereby relaxing the overclosure bound. If the damping grows with the oscillation amplitude, it can also drive different initial amplitudes onto a common attractor that depends only on the local radiation temperature. This synchronizes the scalar with the adiabatic clock, thus suppressing its isocurvature. The resulting isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by exactly the factor by which damping reduces the abundance, in addition to the relaxation from the larger initial misalignment now allowed. This result holds for any damping rate quadratic in the amplitude, regardless of its temperature dependence.

items.title: Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that a scalar whose vacuum expectation value (vev) breaks lepton number at the MeV scale, generating the light-neutrino masses through the inverse seesaw, can also serve as the light mediator of self-interacting dark matter. Dark matter is a pseudo-Dirac fermion whose mass splitting arises from the same vev and is predicted to be proportional to the self-interaction coupling times the vev. A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_\chi/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_\chi\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_\chi\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

items.title: Conformal Holographic Dark Energy and the Neutrino-Mass Tension
items.summary: arXiv:2512.03411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent DESI results suggest a preference for evolving dark energy (DE) over a cosmological constant, motivating the exploration of alternative models for the background expansion. These data also lead to neutrino-mass constraints close to the lower bounds permitted by oscillation experiments. In this work, we propose and test a conformal holographic dark energy (CHDE) model in which the DE density depends on a power law of the conformal time, characterized by an exponent $n$. The model introduces one additional parameter relative to $\Lambda$CDM and reduces to it in the limit $n=0$. We confront CHDE with BAO, CMB, and SNe Ia datasets, following the combinations used by DESI, and perform parameter inference in both flat and non-flat cosmologies. We find a consistent preference for $n\simeq -0.25$ to $-0.32$, with uncertainties below $\pm 0.1$, and disfavor the $\Lambda$CDM limit at the $4.4$--$4.5\sigma$ level; however, the model-comparison statistics provide no consistent preference for CHDE over $\Lambda$CDM. The resulting neutrino-mass constraints remain compatible with terrestrial limits and yield posterior distributions that peak at positive values, avoiding the negative-mass preference found in $\Lambda$CDM. The CHDE model is therefore consistent with current observational constraints and provides a viable alternative to constant dark energy.

Less is More: Unbiased Galaxy Clustering from Fewer Merger Trees
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Galaxy clustering could strongly constrain galaxy formation models but is rarely used, because the two-point correlation function (2PCF) requires a complete galaxy catalogue at every point in parameter space. Semi-analytic models (SAMs) process each halo merger tree independently, so running a SAM on $m$ of $k$ disjoint partitions of the trees, each spanning the full box, cuts the cost by $k/m$. Because a halo's galaxies are kept or discarded together, one-halo pairs are diluted less than two-halo pairs, and the naive estimate overstates small-scale clustering by a factor $k/m$. We introduce the Sparse and Unbiased Clustering Estimator (SaUCE), which removes this bias with weights set by $m$ and $k$ alone. It has no free parameters, gives exactly unbiased pair counts, and applies to any catalogue built from a random subset of whole haloes and to any pair-count statistic. Running a SAM on 7 per cent of the P-Millennium merger trees, 68 per cent of random selections recover the full-box $\xi(r)$ at $z=0$ to within 0.05 dex in each bin from 0.03 to $30\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, at a density of $10^{-2}\,h^{3}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$: a fourteen-fold computational saving. The required fraction rises with redshift and as the number density falls, is the same for two model variants, and transfers between boxes through the galaxy and pair counts. The scatter, derived in closed form, is strongly correlated between bins, so a likelihood must use the full covariance. A recipe for choosing the fraction makes the 2PCF affordable for model calibration and simulation-based inference.

items.title: Millimeter-Wavelength Constraints on Circular Polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background at Arcminute Scales with the Simons Array
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present constraints on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) circular polarization anisotropy at arcminute angular scales, using dedicated measurements from the Simons Array taken with a quarter-wave plate and rotating half-wave plate. A detection of circular polarization in the CMB would probe a range of proposed generation mechanisms, from Standard Model astrophysics to physics beyond it. At an observing frequency of 90 GHz, we place constraints over the multipole range $300 \leq \ell \leq 2000$, corresponding to angular scales of 5.4-36 arcmin, in bands of width $\Delta \ell = 100$, roughly tripling the highest multipole previously reached by a $V$-mode power spectrum measurement. Within this domain, we constrain the 95% confidence upper bound of $\ell (\ell+1) C_\ell^{VV} / (2\pi)$ to range from ${\sim}22\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 350$ bandpower to ${\sim}3.5\times10^3\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 1950$ bandpower. These limits are derived from ${\sim}2.5$ months of observations of each of two small regions of the sky located away from the Galactic plane, totaling ${\sim}12\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ of effective sky area. Because the methodology of this study marginalizes known foreground contamination, these bounds serve as robust, conservative limits on the true CMB circular polarization signal down to the sensitivity limits of the instrument. Additionally, we provide an experimental and analytical framework for implementing circular polarization observations on other telescopes by utilizing a quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate design.

items.title: OASIS: A Fast Dynamical Halo Finding Algorithm
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent work (Garc\'ia et al. 2023), we advocated for defining a dynamical halo as the collection of particles that orbit their self-generated potential. Here we introduce the Orbiting-mass ASsIgnment Scheme (OASIS), a fast energy-based algorithm for constructing dynamical halo catalogs. Using single-snapshot information, OASIS achieves $\simeq 9\%$ scatter in orbiting mass estimates relative to the SPARTA particle-tracking algorithm. As an illustration of the applications enabled by OASIS, we use the Quijote and Erebos simulation suites to show that the $z=0$ dynamical halo mass function is nearly universal with respect to cosmology, and that it is well described by a modified Press-Schechter form with an effective collapse threshold $\delta_{\rm sc} = 1.54$ at intermediate masses. However, this description fails at high masses.

items.title: Self-Interacting Neutrinos in NEDE and DRMD Cosmologies: Posteriors, profiles and evidence using CLiENT
items.summary:
arXiv:2611.13756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A large number of extensions of the $\Lambda$CDM model have been proposed as solutions to the Hubble tension, but they are almost always tested separately. Combinations of such models are rarely studied, and one reason is that their parameter spaces are very costly to explore with standard methods. Here we study a combination of two models which have each been proposed as a solution: self-interacting neutrinos (SI$
u$) and the dark radiation matter decoupling (DRMD) of hot new early dark energy. The SI$
u$+DRMD model has twelve cosmological parameters, a bimodal posterior in the neutrino self-interaction and several flat directions in parameter space, and it can only be investigated in detail because we use the likelihood emulator CLiENT. With emulators trained on about $3	imes 10^5$ likelihood evaluations per dataset we obtain posteriors, best fits and profile likelihoods for the model and for the models nested within it, and all quoted $\chi^2$ values are calculated with the true likelihood. We use two data combinations, both with and without the SH0ES calibration: a conservative one consisting of Planck, DESI BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more aggressive one in which the small-scale CMB spectra come from ACT and SPT. With the most aggressive combination, the SI$
u$+DRMD model provides a much better fit than either SI$
u$ or DRMD on its own, and its posterior gives $H_0 = 70.94\pm 0.60$ km/s/Mpc. It lowers the $\chi^2$ of $\Lambda$CDM by 27.6, compared with 9.9 for DRMD and 4.0 for SI$
u$, i.e. by more than the sum of the two ($\Delta$AIC = -15.7 relative to DRMD, in terms of the Akaike information criterion). This shows that combined models can fit the data considerably better than the individual models, and it demonstrates the value of being able to analyse such complex models in detail.

items.title: Impact of Primordial Magnetic Field-induced Small-scale Power on Non-linear Structure Formation and Cosmic Reionization
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) can enhance small-scale matter perturbations and alter halo formation and reionization. We evolve PMF-modified initial spectra with collisionless $N$-body simulations and use the halo catalogues as sources for semi-numerical ionization and 21-cm brightness-temperature fields in the saturated spin-temperature limit. We compare $\Lambda$CDM with four PMF models, $B_0=100$, $130$, $150$, and $170\,\mathrm{pG}$, at $n_B=-2.9$. With cosmology and source prescriptions fixed, the PMF models show enhanced small-scale clustering, more early low-mass haloes and earlier reionization. Their volume-averaged reionization midpoints advance by $\Delta z_{50}\simeq0.50$--$2.14$, with changes in ionization morphology and 21-cm power spectra. The Thomson optical depth rises from $\tau_{\rm e}\simeq0.0547$ for $\Lambda$CDM to $0.0595$--$0.0786$. These simulation-relative offsets span $0.66$--$3.28$ times the Planck 2018 uncertainty, $\sigma_\tau=0.0073$, and are not exclusion significances. The common source efficiency $N_{\rm ion}$ is calibrated to a reference history approaching ionization completion near $z\sim6$ and an optical depth close to Planck 2018, without model-specific retuning. We omit subsequent magnetic-field evolution and dissipative magnetic heating. Observational bounds require joint treatment of astrophysical degeneracies and numerical uncertainties.

items.title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.

items.title: First constraints on axion-like particles with SPHEREx data
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first search for axion-like particle dark matter using SPHEREx data. We perform a conservative analysis on the first 16.5 months of SPHEREx data and derive new limits on the mass range $0.496 6.5 \times 10^{25}\,\mathrm{s}$. We are also able to detect several expected emission features at high significance, such as atmospheric He I and the 3.3 $\mu$m PAH feature. We calculate the Cram\'er-Rao bound and compare to sensitivity forecasts, finding that our limits could be improved by more than an order of magnitude with solely methodological improvements.

items.title: Unidentified Sources in the 4FGL-DR4 Fermi-LAT Catalog as Potential Dark Matter Satellites
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The nature of dark matter (DM) remains unknown, standing as one of the most pressing questions in modern physics. We focus on indirect DM detection via gamma-ray emission from annihilating weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). Within the $\Lambda$CDM cosmological framework, the hierarchical assembly of structure predicts a rich population of DM halos and subhalos. If WIMPs compose DM, annihilation inside these subhalos would generate gamma rays that could be detectable by instruments such as the Fermi-LAT. Since 2008, Fermi-LAT has cataloged several thousand of gamma-ray sources, with a third lacking clear astrophysical association. Some of these unassociated sources (unIDs) may actually be dark satellites, i.e., Galactic subhalos not massive enough to retain gas or stars and thus with no counterparts at other wavelengths. Starting from the 14-year Fermi-LAT catalog (4FGL-DR4), we conduct a systematic search for dark satellite candidates among its 2428 unIDs. We first design and apply a series of filters based on expected properties of dark satellites to reduce our sample. Through an exhaustive spectral Fermi-LAT data analysis, we find that none of the remaining unIDs shows a statistically significant preference for a DM interpretation. We place conservative constraints on the $\langle\sigma v\rangle-m_{\chi}$ DM parameter space, which are a factor of 2-3 above the thermal relic cross section value at the lowest WIMP masses in a conservative scenario, and rule out thermally-produced WIMPs below $\sim$50 GeV in the $b\bar{b}$ channel when assuming the sensitivity reach of the method. Our results emphasize the distinctive value of unID-based searches: they yield constraints that complement those derived from classical DM targets, such as dwarf spheroidal galaxies, and probe a unique, cosmologically motivated population of dark satellites otherwise inaccessible to observations.

items.title: TITAN DR1: The Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe - Host Galaxies I: Associations, Redshifts and Derived Properties
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the host-galaxy catalogue for TITAN DR1, a sample of 8378 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) at $z \lesssim 0.15$ -- the largest homogeneous low-redshift SN Ia sample assembled to date. We describe the association of each SN with its host, the compilation of redshifts, measurements of uniform far-ultraviolet to mid-infrared (FUV--MIR) photometry, and the derivation of host properties through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. Combining four host-association methods with manual vetting, we securely identify hosts for 7856 SNe~Ia (93.8\%). We compile host-galaxy spectroscopic redshifts for 5522 objects and provide CMB-frame and peculiar-velocity-corrected redshifts. \rev{PSF-matched} photometry is measured for 7568 host galaxies, including both global fluxes and local optical-only fluxes within a fixed 1.5~kpc aperture centred on the SN; \texttt{Bagpipes} returns successful global fits for \rev{all} hosts and local fits for 7329. Stellar mass and rest-frame $g-z$ colour are robustly measured from optical data alone, whereas reliable estimates of star-formation rate, dust attenuation, and mass-weighted age require broader wavelength coverage to break age--dust degeneracies\rev{, and are reported for 5827 hosts}; in our redshift range, MIR data suffice and far-IR coverage is not required. The hosts span a representative low-redshift galaxy population, with a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)=10.22$ (\rev{60\%} high-mass; $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)>10$), \rev{71\%} star-forming ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{sSFR}/\mathrm{yr}^{-1}) > -10.5$), and an approximately exponential $A_V$ distribution. This catalogue provides the foundation for forthcoming analyses of the luminosity step and the broader role of galaxy environment in SN~Ia standardization and cosmology.

items.title: Helicity Decay to Baryons: The Cosmological Evolution of L_mu-L_tau Gauge Fields and Baryogenesis
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13537v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study baryogenesis from the post-inflationary decay of helical U(1)$_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ gauge fields generated during axion inflation. Assuming that Schwinger pair production is suppressed during inflation, a large helicity-to-entropy ratio $\eta_H$ can be generated while keeping the initial lepton asymmetry just after inflation negligible. After reheating, the dissipation of magnetic helicity sources a lepton asymmetry through the chiral anomaly, which is partially converted into a baryon asymmetry by electroweak sphaleron processes. We find that there are parameter spaces where the observed baryon asymmetry can be generated in both the turbulent and dissipation-dominated regimes of the U(1)$_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ magnetic field evolution. The baryon asymmetry generation in the turbulent regime is, however, dominated by the pre-turbulent nearly frozen regime. We further find that the requirement of successful baryogenesis imposes stronger constraints on the inflationary Hubble parameter and the helicity density generated during axion inflation than the requirement for the gauge-field energy not to backreact on the inflaton dynamics.

items.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
items.summary: arXiv:2611.13583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

items.title: DustER: Dust Extinction with Photometric Red Galaxies
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present DustER, a new method for reconstructing dust reddening maps from photometric galaxy survey data. DustER uses red galaxies as "standard crayons". That is, it relies on the mean color of red-sequence galaxies being independent of their position in the sky. Given the galaxy's redshift, the difference between a galaxy's observed color and its expected color measures the reddening by dust along the galaxy's line of sight. When using photometric galaxy survey data, the method must rely on photometric redshifts, which, combined with selection effects, bias the recovered dust maps. DustER uses a novel approach to characterize and correct for these biases by leveraging the known statistical properties of the distribution of dust around the Milky Way. Testing on simulations, we find that the recovered dust maps are contaminated by large-scale structure. However, when we use the DustER map to deredden and select red-sequence galaxies, we find the resulting two-point function is not contaminated by dust.

items.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

items.title: Beyond Self-Similarity: Reconciling X-Ray Scaling Relations in Galaxy Clusters and Groups
items.summary: arXiv:2606.02719v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction $f_g$ and the temperature variation $f_T$. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts an MCMC-based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters $f_g$ and $f_T$ and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction does not show significant evolution with cosmic time, it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass. On the other hand, the temperature variation shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with $\{f_g, f_T\}$ drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3\sigma$ ($>5 \sigma$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 11 (3) percent (four and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity $Y_{LGT0} = L^{-1} M_g^2 T^{a_L}$, a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of $f_g$ and $f_T$ by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution ($M \sim Y_{LGT0} f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2$), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.

items.title: Compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck low-ell data
items.summary: arXiv:2606.05166v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data, constructed from the SRoll2 likelihood which provides the tightest constraint on the reionization optical depth $\tau$ to date. The non-Gaussian form of CMB low-$\ell$ TT and EE likelihoods makes them incompatible with Fisher matrix analyses that require an analytic Gaussian $\chi^2$, such as the Fisher-bias formalism and Fisher forecasts. We show that the $\chi^2$ of an offset log-normal likelihood takes a Gaussian form in the log-transformed power spectrum amplitudes, and can therefore serve as a proxy for the true Gaussian likelihood of this variable in Fisher matrix analyses, without any explicit change of variables. Building on this, we compress the SRoll2 likelihood into a small number of piecewise offset log-normal functions and validate it against the full SRoll2 likelihood via MCMC combined with Planck and ACT DR6 data, finding excellent agreement across all $\Lambda$CDM parameters and in extended cosmological models. We further demonstrate that Fisher matrix uncertainty estimates from our compressed likelihood agree well with the full MCMC posteriors. We release our compressed likelihood planck-gaussian-lowl, a lightweight Python package incorporating the compressed low-$\ell$ TT likelihood from previous work, allowing a straightforward incorporation of the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ data into any Gaussian-likelihood-based analysis. The package is publicly available at \href{https://github.com/nanoomlee/planck-gaussian-lowl}{github.com/nanoomlee/planck-gaussian-lowl}.

items.title: Margaret Hamilton, computing pioneer who led software development for the Apollo program, dies at 90
items.summary: Over two decades at MIT, Hamilton forged new paths in computer science and engineering. Her groundbreaking work included leading the team that programmed the first computers that took humans to the moon.
items.zh_full: Margaret Hamilton，计算先驱，领导了阿波罗计划的软件开发工作，享年90岁。她在MIT度过了二十多年，在计算机科学与工程领域开辟了新路径。她的开创性工作包括领导团队编写了首批将人类送上月球的计算机程序。

items.title: How to design a space habitat that supports its residents’ mental health
